title: XXXIX-XLIV: ordinary and extraordinary; per se and for another — Cap. 16 COMPLETE
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER SEVENTEEN, On God's executive power, follows. nothing kinder, nothing holier, nothing more just — ye foundation belonging toward all our religion plus consolation — from these things rightly established concerning God's will it can be obscure to none that same nothing stands as better than God. yet ordainable unto good — it stands as lawful toward God to will that same sin should have happened with Him permitting, because belonging toward a joined good — god's will toward another stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which He wills things that same which in a certain respect stand as evil. XLIV. God's will through itself stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God wills things simply good. XLIII. EIGHTH, God's will stands as through itself or toward another plus by means belonging toward accident. XLII. Extraordinary stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God acts beside plus above this order according to His wisdom plus choice — hence miracles. XLI. Ordinary stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God constantly keeps ye order once established by means belonging toward Himself in ye works belonging toward nature plus ye gifts belonging toward grace. XL. SEVENTH, God's will stands as ordinary or extraordinary. XXXIX.
pass_b_english: XXXIX. SEVENTH, God's will is ordinary or extraordinary. XL. Ordinary is that by which God constantly keeps the order once established by Himself in the works of nature and the gifts of grace. XLI. Extraordinary is that by which God acts beside and above this order according to His wisdom and choice — hence miracles.

XLII. EIGHTH, God's will is through itself or for another and by accident. XLIII. God's will through itself is that by which God wills things simply good. XLIV. God's will for another is that by which He wills things which in a certain respect are evil, yet ordainable unto good — it is lawful for God to will that sin should have happened with Him permitting, because of a joined good.

From these things rightly established concerning God's will it can be obscure to none that nothing is better than God, nothing kinder, nothing holier, nothing more just — the foundation of all our religion and consolation. CHAPTER SEVENTEEN, On God's executive power, follows.
source_text: XXXIX. SEPTIMO, voluntas Dei est ordinaria aut extraordinaria. XL. Ordinaria est qua Deus ordinem semel a se constitutum in operibus naturae et donis gratiae constanter servat. XLI. Extraordinaria est qua Deus praeter et supra hunc ordinem pro sua sapientia et arbitrio agit — hinc miracula. XLII. OCTAVO, voluntas Dei est per se aut propter aliud et per accidens. XLIII. Voluntas Dei per se est qua Deus vult quae simpliciter bona sunt. XLIV. Voluntas Dei propter aliud est qua vult quae respectu quodam mala sunt, at ordinabilia in bonum — licet Deo velle ut evenerit peccatum ipso permittente propter bonum conjunctum. Ex his de Dei voluntate probe constitutis nemini obscurum esse potest, Deo nihil esse melius, nihil benignius, nihil sanctius, nihil justius — fundamentum totius religionis et consolationis nostrae. CAPUT DECIMUMSEPTIMUM, De potentia Dei exsequente, sequitur.
